evidence: Ter. Eun. 5.8.27: dōnum et praemium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The main sense of the word (Lewis & Short); also a prize (see award). To reward someone is praemiō afficere aliquem (Quint. 3.6.42) or praemium dare alicui prō rē (Cic. Mur. 8).
What is earned: wages, a fee, rent, and so a reward, often in a bad sense, a bribe or a penalty (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Caes. BG 1.44: magnō praemiō remūnerārī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To pay back a kindness, with the person in the accusative and the gift in the ablative; beneficium remūnerārī, to repay a favour.

phrases.latin: praemiīs etiam, quae capit illa aetās, ēvocētur
phrases.english: let him be coaxed on, too, with rewards such as that age enjoys

phrases.latin: ingrāta es, inquit, ōre quae nostrō caput incolume abstulerīs et mercēdem postulēs
phrases.english: “You are ungrateful,” he said, “to have taken your head safe out of my mouth and then ask for a reward”
